original_description: Build, extend, debug or explain R Shiny apps and dashboards by assembling proven patterns from a bundled catalog of ~170 RStudio Shiny examples (layouts, widgets, reactivity, plots, tables, file upload/download, Rmarkdown reports, modules, dynamic UI, plot brushing/clicking, async, bookmarking, custom JavaScript), modernized to bslib and current Shiny idioms, with a script that smoke-tests the finished app headlessly. Use this whenever the user wants a Shiny app, an interactive R dashboard, a web front-end for an R analysis, or asks how to do something in Shiny (add a download button, tabs, filters, a reactive, a module, a map, an upload form, a progress bar), even if they don't say "Shiny" but are working in R and want something interactive in a browser. Also use for Shiny teaching material and for fixing broken Shiny code.

final_description: Use this skill whenever the work touches R Shiny code or should produce one: any mention of shiny, app.R, ui.R/server.R, input$/output$, reactive(), modules or bslib, or any request for an interactive browser dashboard, explorer or tool in R for colleagues, students or a lab, even when "Shiny" is never named. Covers building an app from a CSV or data frame with filters, dropdowns, date ranges, value boxes, plots and tables; refactoring or splitting large apps into modules; upgrading old Shiny code (shinythemes, callModule, shinydashboard) to bslib; plot click, hover or brush and other interactivity; and diagnosing Shiny errors such as reactive-context failures. Invoke it before writing or editing the code, even for small fixes. It includes tested templates and a checker that catches broken UI/server wiring. Skip it for Python dashboards, BI tools, static plots, standalone HTML widgets and non-Shiny R analysis.

history.description: R Shiny expert toolkit. Load this skill FIRST for any task that writes, changes, reviews or debugs Shiny code, since it holds tested patterns, current bslib idioms and a headless checker for UI/server ID mismatches. Use it for: building a browser app or dashboard in R from a CSV or data frame (dropdowns, filters, date ranges, value boxes, charts, tables, downloads); splitting big app.R files into modules; migrating legacy code (shinythemes, callModule, shinydashboard, ui.R/server.R) to bslib; click, hover or brush on ggplot; dynamic UI, progress bars, async, bookmarking, custom JS; fixing Shiny errors such as reactive-context or 'object not found'; teaching Shiny. Also use when an R user wants colleagues or students to explore data interactively, even without saying "Shiny". Not for Python (Streamlit, Dash), Power BI, static ggplot figures, standalone plotly HTML or R package setup.
